decisions.reason: The adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display builds directly on the firm's core cardboard design and production know-how, so it can interpret customer feedback and keep refining the product.
A cardboard shelf display with a pegboard back is a modest variation on the firm's established display competence and fits its in-house design and manufacturing capabilities.
The standard cardboard quarter-pallet display is a staple of the firm's knowledge base and customer demand, making it a low-risk product to keep.
The eighth-pallet cardboard display uses the same related knowledge and production processes as the firm's core range, so the firm can learn from it and adapt it easily.

The wooden pallet is further from the firm's cardboard-based knowledge and harder to improve in-house, but it complements the one-stop display offering, so the firm keeps it for now while dropping it is a real possibility.
The media-specific quarter-pallet display relies on core cardboard competence, though its niche segment may shrink, so it is kept with moderate risk.
